params.body:
The meeting of 20 August asked for the information to be exportable to Excel, and left open whether per day, per site or per worker. There was no export of the worksheets themselves, only CSVs of Verkennen, Netwerk and Overdracht.

## What changes

**A workbook per period.** `GET /werkfiches/excel?van=&tot=` (office login) downloads a real `.xlsx`, one sheet per kind:

| Sheet | One row per | Columns |
|---|---|---|
| Per dag | worksheet | date, worker, profile, sites, hours, break, departure, return, plate, odometer, status, confirmed at, number of signals, what is missing |
| Uren per werf | line | date, worker, profile, site code, site, from, until, hours, work done, his words, status |
| Machines | machine | date, worker, profile, sites of the day, machine, hours, his words |
| Materiaal | material | date, worker, profile, sites of the day, article code, material, quantity, unit |
| Signalen | signal | date, worker, profile, sites of the day, type, description, urgency, resolved |

- **Per day, per site or per worker.** Every row carries the date, the worker and the sites, so the office can answer any of the three with a filter or a pivot instead of us choosing one.
- **Formatting.** Headers are bold and stay in view, with a filter on them. Hours and quantities are numbers, not text.
- **What counts.** Empty drafts are left out. Hours per day are computed from the lines minus the break, as the sheet computes them.
- **Filters and limits.** Optional `werknemer` and `werf` filter the period. A period is at most a year.

**On the day overview.** "Excel van deze week" next to the date picker, and "Andere periode" for any from-to (by default the month up to the day shown).

**Code.**
- `App\Export\Xlsx` is a small writer on `ZipArchive`: inline strings, numbers, a bold frozen header, an autofilter, column widths. No dependency.
- If the server has no zip extension, the route falls back to a CSV of the hours per site.
- `App\Export\WorksheetExport` builds the sheets.

## Tests

- `WorksheetExportTest` covers:
  - a confirmed week becomes a workbook with the five sheets;
  - 7 hours for two blocks;
  - escaped text, and numbers as numbers;
  - an empty draft left out;
  - only the office can download;
  - the day overview offers the week.
- Full suite green.
- A workbook built from a copy of the production-size database was read back with ExcelJS: all five sheets, headers and rows as expected.
